instruction:
Use Abaqus/CAE via the Command Line Interface (CLI) or Python scripting environment to perform a tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system.

Part:
Instantiate a 3D Deformable Shell part. Sketch a rectangle on the XY plane with dimensions 120 mm in the X direction and 240 mm in the Y direction. Cut a circular hole at the center point (60, 120) mm with a diameter of 12 mm.

Property:
Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with thickness 1 mm and 5 through-thickness integration points. Assign the section to the entire plate geometry.

Assembly:
Create one dependent instance of the shell plate.

Step:
Create a Static, General step named Step-HoleTension, placing it after the Initial step.

Loads and Boundary Conditions:
Apply shell edge loads of 8 N/mm to the two vertical outer edges. On the left edge at X = 0, apply the load in the global negative X direction. On the right edge at X = 120, apply the load in the global positive X direction.

To prevent rigid-body motion without over-constraining the tensile deformation:
- At the bottom-left corner (0, 0), constrain U1 = U2 = U3 = 0.
- At the bottom-right corner (120, 0), constrain U2 = U3 = 0.
- At the top-left corner (0, 240), constrain U3 = 0.

Mesh:
Seed the circular hole edge with an approximate element size of 2.4 mm. Apply a global seed size of 10 mm to the plate. Assign element type S4R and generate the mesh.

Job:
Create a job named Job-FlangeHole, submit it, and wait for successful completion.

Save:
Save the model database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.cae. Ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.odb.
